cases.title: object keys are sorted, recursively; list order is kept
no whitespace; slashes and non-ASCII are written as they are, never escaped
U+2028 and U+2029 are written raw, as JSON.stringify writes them
cases.notes: PHP escapes these by default; JSON.stringify does not. The flag JSON_UNESCAPED_LINE_TERMINATORS makes the two agree.

cases.title: control characters, quotes and backslashes are escaped the JSON way
keys sort by UTF-8 BYTES: "Z" < "a" < "\u{00E9}" < "\u{FF61}" < an astral key
cases.notes: Discriminates a port that sorts with the default JavaScript comparison (UTF-16 code units), which puts the astral key (a surrogate pair, 0xD83D...) BEFORE U+FF61.

cases.title: a float is refused, because PHP and JavaScript do not print floats the same way
an empty object stays {} and an empty list stays []
cases.notes: JSON decoders in PHP lose the difference; `objects` names the paths that are objects.

cases.title: integers, booleans and null print as JSON literals
hash = sha256(prev_hash + "\n" + canonical({seq, envelope_id, at, type, actor, source, ip, user_agent, data})), from the genesis of 64 zeros
empty data hashes as an empty OBJECT, {}
cases.notes: A port that hashes [] for empty data agrees with nothing PHP wrote.

cases.title: the IP and user agent are inside the hash
a client-reported page view hashes its source
the first event has seq 1 and the genesis as prev_hash
the next event takes seq + 1 and the previous hash
a type outside the closed event set is refused
page.viewed must come from the client: a server page view is refused
every event but page.viewed is server-observed: a client signer.signed is refused
cases.notes: The evidence rule: a browser can claim it showed a page, never that someone signed.

cases.title: an intact chain verifies and reports its head
an empty chain is intact, with the genesis as its head
a missing row is a sequence_gap at the seq found
a prev_hash that is not the previous hash is a broken_link
changed data is a hash_mismatch at that row
a changed IP address is a hash_mismatch
data read raw from a store as a JSON string verifies the same
a row from another envelope's chain fails (hash_mismatch or broken_link, never ok)
rewriting a row and recomputing ITS hash breaks the link to the next row
an object whose keys are "0", "1" stays an object
cases.notes: PHP's json_decode(assoc: true) turns this into the list ["a","b"]. Canonical JSON is over JSON values, so it must not.

cases.title: the list with the same values stays a list
index-keyed objects nested in objects and lists stay objects
event data with index-like keys hashes as an object
a chain whose data is an index-keyed object, read raw as a JSON string, verifies
cases.notes: The raw-store form: data as the JSON text a database column holds. A reader that decodes it into a list computes another hash.

cases.title: signer.requested_changes is in the closed set, server-observed, with its text
a request for changes reported by the client is refused: the server observes it
